split_reasoning: Assigning duties and responsibilities is one activity with a common output: a project work assignment.

parts.text: Assign project duties and responsibilities to project personnel.
parts.type_reasoning: Each assignment produces a work allocation that team members can act on.
parts.unit_reasoning: An assignment to a person or team is a practical unit communicated and relied on as a whole.
parts.start: a project duty or responsibility needs an owner
parts.end: the assignment is recorded or communicated to the responsible personnel
parts.checked_by: assigned personnel and the project manager
parts.overlap_reasoning: Work assignments can form part of activity scheduling or staffing in a project plan, but also cover individual responsibilities.

split_reasoning: One activity: gathering requirements from stakeholders, followed by writing them down; split live elicitation from documenting.

parts.text: Meet or talk with key stakeholders to learn their requirements and objectives.
parts.type_reasoning: The value is in the live conversation.

parts.text: Write up the project requirements and objectives gathered from stakeholders.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces a requirements document stakeholders confirm.
parts.unit_reasoning: One requirements document or summary per project or phase.

split_reasoning: One activity: talking with team to find and fix problems.

parts.text: Confer with project personnel to identify and resolve problems.
parts.type_reasoning: Done in live conversations; nothing separate is produced.

split_reasoning: One activity: building a status presentation; delivering it is covered by the reporting statements.

parts.text: Create a project status presentation for customers or the team.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces a slide deck others review.
parts.unit_reasoning: One deck is prepared per status meeting.
parts.start: status review meeting scheduled and data gathered
parts.end: deck ready and sent or presented

notes: Delivery of the presentation is live and is treated as part of the meeting.

split_reasoning: One activity: writing or revising the project plan.

parts.text: Develop or update the project plan covering objectives, technologies, schedule, funding and staffing.
parts.type_reasoning: The plan is a document the team and sponsor rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: One plan or one plan revision is issued as a whole.
parts.work_item: one project plan or plan update
parts.start: project starts or change requires an update

split_reasoning: One activity: analysing objectives and schedule to list needed resources.

parts.text: Identify the resources, staff and funding a project needs from its objectives and schedule.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces a needs list that others approve and act on.
parts.unit_reasoning: One needs assessment per project or phase.

split_reasoning: One activity: choosing vendors or consultants for a project need.

parts.text: Identify, review and select a vendor or consultant for a project need.
parts.type_reasoning: Each selection ends in a recommended or chosen vendor.
parts.unit_reasoning: Each vendor selection runs from need to choice.

split_reasoning: One activity: checking spend against budget.

parts.text: Review costs incurred by project staff against the budget to spot budget issues.
parts.type_reasoning: Each review ends in flagged issues that others act on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Cost reviews are done each period.
parts.work_item: one periodic cost review against budget

split_reasoning: One activity: tracking milestones and deliverables.

parts.text: Track project milestones and deliverables and flag slippage.
parts.type_reasoning: Each tracking cycle produces an updated tracker and flagged items.
parts.unit_reasoning: Tracking is done per reporting cycle.
parts.work_item: one milestone and deliverable tracking update

split_reasoning: Monitoring performance can produce a documented assessment, while delivering feedback is a separate live interaction.

parts.text: Assess and document a project team member's performance for feedback.
parts.type_reasoning: A documented assessment is a discrete output used to support feedback.
parts.unit_reasoning: An assessment of one team member for a review period or feedback occasion is a coherent item.
parts.start: performance information for a team member is available for review
parts.end: observations are recorded or prepared for feedback
parts.overlap_reasoning: Project updates may provide evidence for the assessment, but reviewing updates to meet deadlines has a different purpose.

parts.text: Give a project team member performance feedback.
parts.type_reasoning: The value of feedback is in the live discussion with the team member.
parts.overlap_reasoning: A feedback discussion can address project problems, but problem-solving discussions need not be performance feedback.

notes: Feedback may be informal and not accompanied by a separate written assessment; shares are estimates.

split_reasoning: One activity: negotiating terms with parties.

parts.text: Negotiate with stakeholders or suppliers to get resources or materials.
parts.type_reasoning: The value is in live negotiation.

split_reasoning: One activity: planning and coordinating activities, mostly by building and managing the schedule.

parts.text: Plan and schedule project activities to meet deadlines.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces a schedule that the team follows.
parts.unit_reasoning: One schedule or schedule revision per planning cycle.
parts.work_item: one project schedule or schedule revision

parts.text: Coordinate project activities day to day with team members.
parts.type_reasoning: Live coordination.

split_reasoning: Joins three reports, budget estimates, progress reports and cost tracking reports; these are different documents.

parts.text: Prepare and submit a budget estimate.
parts.type_reasoning: Estimate document is reviewed and approved.
parts.unit_reasoning: One estimate per project or change.

parts.text: Prepare and submit a progress report.
parts.type_reasoning: Report is read by managers.
parts.unit_reasoning: One report per period.

parts.text: Prepare and submit a cost tracking report.
parts.type_reasoning: Report is read by finance and sponsor.
parts.unit_reasoning: One report per period.

split_reasoning: One activity: producing and sending project documents.

parts.text: Produce and distribute a project document.
parts.type_reasoning: Each document is handed to the team or client.
parts.unit_reasoning: Documents are produced and sent one at a time.
parts.work_item: one project document produced and distributed

split_reasoning: Proposing a plan modification and reviewing or approving a proposed modification are distinct activities with different outputs.

parts.text: Propose a modification to a project plan.
parts.type_reasoning: A proposed change is a discrete item submitted for consideration.
parts.unit_reasoning: A change proposal is reviewed as a whole by the person or group authorized to decide.
parts.start: a need to change the project plan is identified
parts.end: the proposed modification and its rationale are submitted for review
parts.checked_by: project manager, sponsor, or change authority
parts.overlap_reasoning: An approved proposal may lead to a plan update and may be distributed as a project document, but the proposal is a distinct decision input.

parts.text: Review or approve a proposed modification to a project plan.
parts.type_reasoning: Each review produces a recommendation or decision on a proposed change.
parts.unit_reasoning: The proposed modification is the unit reviewed and decided upon.
parts.work_item: one proposed project plan modification reviewed or approved
parts.start: a proposed plan modification is received for review
parts.end: the review recommendation or approval decision is recorded and communicated
parts.checked_by: project manager, sponsor, or change authority
parts.overlap_reasoning: Reviewing a modification can lead to updating the plan, but a decision is distinct from issuing the updated plan.

notes: Shares vary with the worker's authority to propose and approve changes.

split_reasoning: One activity: filling a staffing need.

parts.text: Recruit and hire a project team member.
parts.type_reasoning: Each hire ends in an offer and a staffed role.
parts.unit_reasoning: Each position is filled individually.

notes: Interviews are live; treated within the hiring unit.

split_reasoning: Project status is reported both in written updates and in live discussions with managers.

parts.text: Send managers a written update on project status.
parts.type_reasoning: A written status update is a discrete communication that managers rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: One update for a reporting period or request is sent and read as a whole.
parts.work_item: one written project status update to managers
parts.start: a manager requests an update or a reporting interval arrives
parts.end: the status update is sent to managers
parts.overlap_reasoning: A written update may take the form of a progress or cost report, presentation, or other project document, while this target also covers other status communications.

parts.text: Brief managers live on project status.
parts.type_reasoning: The briefing is a live exchange in which managers can discuss status and issues.
parts.overlap_reasoning: A briefing may occur in a project meeting or use a status presentation, but those statements also cover scheduling, facilitation, and preparation.

notes: The written and live shares vary by reporting practice.

split_reasoning: One activity: asking for and checking updates.

parts.text: Ask team members for updates and review them to confirm deadlines will be met.
parts.type_reasoning: Each cycle produces a checked status that others rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Updates are collected per cycle.
parts.work_item: one round of project updates requested and reviewed

split_reasoning: Joins scheduling meetings (a small deliverable) with facilitating them (live).

parts.text: Schedule a project meeting.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces an invitation attendees rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: One invite per meeting.
parts.work_item: one meeting scheduled and invitation sent

parts.text: Facilitate a project meeting.
parts.type_reasoning: Value is in the live meeting.

split_reasoning: One activity: delivering finished work to the client after quality checks.

parts.text: Check a deliverable meets quality standards and submit it to the client.
parts.type_reasoning: Each deliverable is handed to the client who accepts it.
parts.unit_reasoning: Deliverables are submitted as a whole one at a time.
parts.work_item: one project deliverable checked and submitted
